Rolls the signal off below the frequency set here, 20Hz to 500Hz at 12dB per octave, and the filter is out of circuit at 20Hz; the panel prints LPF but this knob is the high-pass
Inverts both channels, and lights amber while the inversion is on
The left input, and the source for the right channel as well while the right input is unpatched
The right input; with nothing patched here the left input feeds this channel too
The left channel after the two filters, the phase invert and the gain
The right channel after the two filters, the phase invert and the gain
Note — The three small squares under the meter choose what it shows: RMS, VU with a 300ms decay, or PPM.
Note — The small square at the top right of the meter turns the meter display off; the LED bar graph beside the knobs keeps working.
Note — Each jack carries one channel, so a polyphonic cable is reduced to its first channel.
Note — CHI-X adds voltage control of the gain, both filters and the phase invert, and has to be placed immediately to the right of this module.

ChanIn.notes: The panel labels HPF and LPF are on the wrong filters: the knob printed HPF is HIGH_CUT_PARAM, 1kHz to 20kHz, set as a low-pass (src/ChanIn.cpp:1003, 1731, label at 1585, ChanInFilters::updateFiltersIfChanged AeLOWPASS), and the knob printed LPF is LOW_CUT_PARAM, 20Hz to 500Hz, set as a high-pass. The README describes the two ranges correctly and never connects them to the panel lettering. The filters are bypassed entirely while the high cut is at 20kHz and the low cut at 20Hz, which are the defaults, so the module starts as gain and phase only. DISPLAY_ENABLE_PARAM has no ParamWidget and cannot be clicked for help; it is toggled by a custom square drawn at 96,43.

ChanInCV.notes: The filter CVs are tested with `!= 0.0f` rather than by whether the jack is patched, and when non-zero they replace the knob: the frequency becomes the geometric centre of the range multiplied by two to the power of the volts. Those centres are not stored as such; they are the log2 constants LPF_CENTER_LOG and HPF_CENTER_LOG in src/ChanIn.cpp:931-932, which are log2(4472.14) and log2(100). The expander writes its HPF jack into msg->hpfFreqCV and CHAN-IN reads that field into its low-pass CV (src/ChanIn.cpp:1181-1182, commented `Swapped`); the two swaps cancel, so the jack printed HPF really does move the knob printed HPF. The PHASE jack has no attenuverter. The expander is inert unless CHAN-IN is the module immediately to its left.

Shape.notes: PUNCH is not an attack control. The README says "PUNCH control: 0% to 100% (attack time: 0%=5ms slow, 100%=0.1ms fast/punchy)"; in the code the knob value is loaded into punchEnvelope on every closed-to-open transition and the gain becomes smoothedGain * (1 + punchEnvelope), decaying with a 15ms time constant (src/Shape.cpp:226-227, 240, 296). Attack time comes only from the menu slider, 0.1ms to 25ms. The GATE knob is marked in dB but the mapping is linear in voltage: (dB + 60)/60 times 80% of the reference, so -60dB is 0V and 0dB is 4V at the 5V reference (src/Shape.cpp:171-176). The sidechain is chosen by getChannels() > 0, which is the same test as isConnected() here. The gate attenuation meter is driven from the left channel only (src/Shape.cpp:835).

C1EQ.notes: The panel prints EQUALIZER; the module browser calls it C1-EQ. Both outer bands default to Cut (B1_MODE_PARAM and B4_MODE_PARAM default 2), and the mode-change branch fires on the first process() because lastB1Mode starts at -1, so a freshly added module has its LF frequency written to 20Hz and its HF frequency to 20kHz and both those GAIN knobs pinned at 0dB by setValue every sample (src/C1EQ.cpp:1230-1233, 1556-1586). Turning either GAIN knob while C is chosen does nothing, and the knob springs back. The param values run 0 Shelf, 1 Bell, 2 Cut, and are inverted again inside updateBandCoefficients as 2 - rawMode; the C, B, S lamps are wired to match the panel. LF and HF Q are hardcoded at 0.8 and 1.0 (src/C1EQ.cpp:1400-1404) and at 0.707 in cut mode. The oversampling factor is chosen from the sample rate rather than being fixed; the README's "typically 4x" is not a constant in the code. ANALYSER_ENABLE_PARAM has no ParamWidget and cannot be clicked for help.

C1COMP.notes: AUTO release is unreachable. src/C1COMP.cpp:999 clamps the knob plus any CV to a maximum of 0.89, and line 1000 then tests `releaseRaw >= 0.9f`, which can never be true; setAutoRelease(true) is called nowhere else in the file. The comment on line 998 says the clamp is there so that CV modulation preserves access to AUTO, but the clamp is applied whether or not an expander is present. The top 11% of the knob is therefore a dead zone holding the release at about 1167ms, while ReleaseParamQuantity prints AUTO there and the README lists "plus AUTO mode". The THRESHOLD knob is a 0 to 1 parameter displayed as -20dB to +10dB. The four squares above the display write compressorType directly and the engine is rebuilt when process() notices the change. DISPLAY_ENABLE_PARAM has no ParamWidget and cannot be clicked for help.

ChanOut.notes: DRIVE and CHAR are both inert on the default settings. ChanOutCleanEngine::process takes drive but computes driveAmount = (outputMode == 1) ? drive * 0.1f : 0.0f (src/ChanOutCleanEngine.hpp:117-125), so in Master Output mode, which is the default, the knob does nothing; in Channel Output mode full drive is a gain of 1.1, about 0.83dB. The clean engine's process() takes no character argument at all (src/ChanOut.cpp:845-847), so CHAR is read by nothing on the Standard engine. The pan law is the other way round from the README, which says Master is linear and Channel is equal power: applyPan uses cos/sin in both modes and multiplies by sqrt(2) only in Channel mode, so Master loses 3dB at centre and Channel is unity at centre (src/ChanOut.cpp, applyPan). The character engines are selected by four custom squares as well as by the menu. DISPLAY_ENABLE_PARAM has no ParamWidget and cannot be clicked for help. The mute and dim slews are both 125 units per second.
